messages:
jordan-sales: Quick sync — Pillar Health wants a POC run next week. They care about 95th/99th tail latency under sustained 300 qps, coldstart behavior, and KMS-backed keys for embeddings. Can ops help with a runbook and rough cost estimate?

alex-eng: Yep. We should do two profiles: hosted (standard) and dedicated (reserved GPUs). For hosted, expect ~50% higher per-token cost but simpler infra. For dedicated, we can hit lower unit cost at steady load; need node count and autoscale policy.

maria-ops: I'll draft the runbook. Question: what's the target sequence length and average tokens per request? That drives batching and KV cache behavior.

jordan-sales: They sent a sample: avg 220 tokens in, 130 tokens generated. 75% of requests are chat-style with short context reuse (same user session).

alex-eng: Ok that favors prefix caching. For 300 qps sustained with 220/130, estimate peak token/s ~ 300*(220+130)=~105k tokens/s. With our quantized 8-bit medium model on A100-equivalent, rough throughput per GPU ~12k tokens/s. So we'd need ~9 GPUs to meet sustained throughput with headroom.

samir-sre: For tail SLOs (95th < 300ms, 99th < 600ms) we should do continuous batching cap at 20ms and KV cache enabled. Also multi-AZ routing to avoid regional noisy neighbor spikes.

kori-qa: I'll create the acceptance test harness. Plan to run 30m steady-state followed by 10m microbursts (3x peak) to validate autoscale and tail. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and coldstart latencies.

jordan-sales: Pricing ask from Pillar: provide a ballpark monthly committed price for Dedicated to satisfy procurement. They want a 12mo commitment number and a 1mo hosted PoC number.

maria-ops: Ballpark: Dedicated (9 GPUs, reserved): $Xk/month (ie compute + infra + support). Hosted PoC (1 month, fully managed, burstable): higher per-token; estimate ~$Yk for the 30m run + sampling and storage. I'll put numbers in the runbook draft.

alex-eng: Also highlight cost levers: lower quantization (4-bit), smaller context window, and prefix caching + session affinity will cut token/s and effective GPUs. We'll show sensitivity table in the deck.

samir-sre: Security note — Pillar requires KMS-managed customer key for embedding vectors and audit logs. kms-bot: "KMS CHECK: We have a customer-managed KMS integration ready in Private and Dedicated planes. Hosted supports envelope encryption; for true CMK, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment."

jordan-sales: Good — add that to the SOW options. Procurement will want TOC for keys and egress.

kori-qa: Runbook draft:
```
- Prep: spin up 9-dedicated GPUs with autoscale min 6 / max 12 (scale by token/s), enable KV caching and continuous batching.
- Traffic generator: session-aware Poisson arrival to mimic 75% session reuse, seed with sample traces.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, GPU util, queueing tail, coldstart time, error rate.
- Burst test: 10m at 900 qps.
- Coldstart: 5 sequential restarts during soak to capture warmup curves.
- Security: test KMS key rotation during run and verify audit log entries.
```

maria-ops: Nice. I'll add operational playbook for fallback: route to smaller spec model (lower cost variant) if latency > SLO for >2min. Also pre-warm policy: keep one standby node to limit coldstarts during microbursts.

alex-eng: For measurements, we'll include a control run on hosted medium cluster (auto-managed capacity) to show delta in tail and unit cost. Expect hosted to have slightly higher p95 but similar p50.

jordan-sales: Can we get a one-page summary for the execs after run with numbers and recommended contract terms?

maria-ops: Yep, I'll produce: 1) summary table (p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, cost per 1M tokens), 2) recommended commit level, 3) security summary (KMS, audit), 4) risk/mitigations.

kori-qa: Timeline: runbook finalized by Mon EOD, infra ready Tue, POC run Wed-Thu, analysis Fri. I'll run the harness and post results.

jordan-sales: Perfect. One last ask — Pillar asked about performance degradation when KMS calls occur. Alex — any estimate?

alex-eng: If embedding calls block on synchronous KMS calls, expect ~10-20ms added per embedding request depending on KMS region. We'll recommend async wrapping or client-side transient keys to avoid stressing critical path. Note that for Dedicated with CMK in same VPC, latencies should be low (~5-10ms).

samir-sre: I'll schedule a brief security-comms with Pillar's security lead to confirm key rotation windows.

jordan-sales: Thanks team — I'll update Pillar and loop in procurement. Kori, ping the thread when full run results are in. :thumbsup:
